name: OAuth2 provider adapter
purpose: The pluggable seam that turns a project-authored provider record into the resolved shape the flow controller uses on every step. Owns per-record validation at boot, provider lookup by id at flow initiation, and the JWKS fetching port the id_token verifier reads through. Does NOT own the state machine and does NOT own session issue; those are the flow controller (TAC-1101) and the session-bridge (TAC-1103) respectively.
responsibilities: Load the provider-config module at boot and validate every record: required fields present, `flow=authorisation-code-pkce`, `providerKind` in {`oidc`, `oauth2-only`}, OIDC providers carry `issuer` and `jwksUri`, records with `providerLogout='redirect'` carry `endSessionEndpoint` (AC-10108-3, AC-10109-2, REQ-002, REQ-008).

Refuse boot on a malformed record with a stable-coded error naming the provider id and the missing or invalid field; audit event `oauth2.provider_config_refused` carries provider id and reason class (AC-10108-3).
Expose `resolve(providerId) -> record | absent`; return `absent` for an unknown id and let the flow controller emit OAUTH2_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN (AC-10109-2).

Expose `fetchJwks(providerId) -> { keys[] }` with a cache keyed by provider id whose TTL is `jwksCacheTtlSeconds` (default 900); refresh on cache miss or on a verifier hint that a key is unknown (AC-10105-1, AC-10105-2).
Never expose `clientSecret` on the client-tier record form; the client-tier record carries a redacted placeholder and the server-tier record carries the real value (REQ-002).
internalStructure: One factory function producing an adapter closure over an injected `providerConfig` module (a plain data record set) and an injected `httpFetch` port (the process's HTTP client, either the platform's `fetch` or an injected mock in tests). The JWKS cache is a Map keyed by provider id whose value is `{ keys[], fetchedAt }`; TTL eviction is on read. The validator is a pure function invoked once at boot per record.

interfaces.name: providerConfig
interfaces.description: The project-authored provider-config module exposing `list() -> record[]`. Each record is a plain object with the fields declared in REQ-002 and REQ-008. Server-tier records carry `clientSecret`; client-tier records carry a redacted placeholder.

interfaces.name: httpFetch
interfaces.description: The process's HTTP-fetch port used for JWKS fetch; injected so the test harness can substitute an in-process mock that returns the mock provider's JWKS.

tradeoffs: Fixing the record shape and validating at boot fails fast on misconfigured providers rather than at the moment a real operator tries to sign in; the trade is a slightly larger boot-time surface for the operator to fix and a much smaller failure window at operate time. Caching JWKS costs the process a small piece of memory per provider and buys the id_token verifier a cheap read on every callback; the TTL and the miss-refresh path bound the staleness at `jwksCacheTtlSeconds + one callback`. Not owning the state machine keeps this TAC's surface narrow enough that a new provider vendor is a config-record write, not a code change here.
